decision: Can an AI agent buying for a customer read, compare and transact with us today, and what blocks it first?
limitations: It is a self-assessment, not a crawl. It scores the flags you pass and cannot check the live site; verify each answer with view-source or curl.
Each check is pass or fail, so a half-done item scores nothing. Rendering is a hard gate: without --ssr the verdict is BLOCKED whatever else passes.
It measures whether an agent can evaluate and act, not whether AI engines cite you. Use seo-geo-aeo-audit for that.
It reads --flags or {"checks": {id: true/false}}. Unknown flags or ids, non-true/false values and stray arguments stop the run with an error that names them.
review: Whoever owns the website verifies each flag against the live site (raw HTML, robots.txt, a no-login purchase path), and the founder makes the published-pricing and AI-crawler decisions explicitly before fixes are scheduled.
